DELETE → HTTP 204; session row gone=True; device-sessions object gone=True; derived recording survived=True; audit table found=False || DEFECT: deleting the session did NOT delete the recording it produced. deleteSession() removes the sate_device_sessions row and its object in the device-sessions bucket, but the derived `recordings` row (e325c7c6-33ef-4bd0-99c1-bb28d72dfd40) and its copy of the audio in the recordings bucket (bc324864-51a6-4328-be68-d7b0dadaabce/1788749956355_device_SATE-443EAC_s92.wav) both survive. The take still appears in the web app and the audio is still downloadable, so 'delete' does not delete the clinical data — the opposite of what a retention/erasure request needs. ; no audit-trail table is reachable (sate_audit_log=404, audit_log=404, sate_events=404, session_audit=404) — deletions and retries leave no auditable record, which SEC-007 and BE-012 both require.

edit saved=True updated_at bumped=False; server-side version columns=none; history tables found=False || DEFECT: `recordings.updated_at` did not change when the transcript was rewritten — the column exists but nothing maintains it, so even 'when was this last edited' is not answerable from the row. ; the edit overwrites `recordings.transcript` in place. There is no version column and no history table (recording_versions=404, transcript_versions=404, recording_history=404, transcript_history=404). Undo/redo lives only in the browser's localStorage (`historyService.ts`, key `transcript_history_<id>`, capped at 50 states), so history is per-browser, invisible to anyone else, and lost on cache clear, a different device, or another user opening the same recording. WEB-005 asks for versioning of a saved transcript; the server keeps exactly one version.

A→HTTP 200, B→HTTP 200 against the same pre-image; winner='writer B'; conflict detected=False; malformed save→HTTP 400 || DEFECT: writer B's save (HTTP 200) silently overwrote writer A's — final text is 'writer B'. Saves go straight to PostgREST with no version check, no If-Match/ETag and no updated_at precondition, so two clinicians editing the same transcript lose one set of edits with no warning and no way to recover it (there is no server-side history to recover from).
/sessions/raw (the pre-chunking upload path, no `total`, no `flags`) is still accepted by device-api v21+ → HTTP 200. Legacy firmware keeps uploading.

the upload API carries NO client timestamp — created_at is the database's own UTC default, so a wrong recorder clock cannot skew stored time (observed skew 14s). DST is not representable: storage is UTC throughout.
